name: university-v1
notes: Predictions are hand-written to stand in for the failure modes a text-to-SQL model actually produces: paraphrases that are semantically identical, near-misses that drop a predicate or a join condition, and the occasional non-query. The point of the suite is the gap between the two metrics, so the equivalent-but-reworded cases are deliberate, not padding.

cases.question: How many students have a GPA above 3.5?
cases.gold: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students WHERE gpa > 3.5
cases.prediction: SELECT COUNT(1) AS n FROM students s WHERE s.gpa > 3.5

cases.question: List the names of students in Computer Sciences.
cases.gold: SELECT s.name FROM students s JOIN departments d ON s.dept_id = d.id WHERE d.name = 'Computer Sciences'
cases.prediction: SELECT students.name FROM departments JOIN students ON departments.id = students.dept_id WHERE departments.name = 'Computer Sciences'

cases.question: Which course titles has at least one student enrolled in?
cases.gold: SELECT title FROM courses WHERE id IN (SELECT course_id FROM enrollments)
cases.prediction: SELECT c.title FROM courses c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e WHERE e.course_id = c.id)

cases.question: Which students are in years 2 through 3?
cases.gold: SELECT name FROM students WHERE year >= 2 AND year <= 3
cases.prediction: SELECT name FROM students WHERE year BETWEEN 2 AND 3

cases.question: List each instructor with their department name.
cases.gold: SELECT i.name, d.name FROM instructors i JOIN departments d ON i.dept_id = d.id
cases.prediction: SELECT i.name, d.name FROM instructors i, departments d WHERE i.dept_id = d.id
